competency_fulfillment.rationale: All 17 samples are addition problems set in a money context and every total is correct: seed 602 'What is the total value of 1 ₱500 bill, 1 ₱20 bill, and 2 ₱1 coins?' keys 522, seed 44 keys 506, seed 50 keys 205, and the error_detect item at seed 55 correctly flags 'Grace says the answer is 37' as wrong with 27 as the true total. Every item is answerable from what is printed: the cloze items at seeds 50, 601 and 603 render the whole sentence with no ___, so no operand is blanked out.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sentence names four things: sums up to 1000, money problems, with regrouping, and without regrouping. Money is present in all 17 samples and the without-regrouping case is abundant, for example seed 43 with 28 and 30. The with-regrouping case is almost absent. Working each sample by column, only seed 502 'What is the total value of 1 ₱10 coin and 2 ₱5 coins?' forces a carry, because 5 plus 5 makes 10; the other 16 are carry-free, including the largest ones such as seed 602 and seed 44. One marginal item is thin evidence for a sub-case the competency names explicitly. Separately, the word including implies money is a subset, yet no non-money addition problem appears in the set.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: One-step totals with values a Grade 2 Quarter 2 pupil can hold. The three-addend denomination items, such as seed 44 'What is the total value of 1 ₱500 bill, 1 ₱5 coin, and 1 ₱1 coin?' and seed 500, add counting load without adding any new operation, which is appropriate here. Reading length is short and the question sentence is always last.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four formatters appear: mcq, cloze (seed 50), true_false (seed 51) and error_detect (seeds 55 and 605). Two problem framings appear: a bills-and-coins total, and a denomination tally such as 'What is the total value of 1 ₱10 coin and 2 ₱5 coins?' at seed 502. Redundancy note: seeds 500 and 501 carry the identical question text 'What is the total value of 1 ₱10 coin, 1 ₱5 coin, and 3 ₱1 coins?' and differ only in formatter, so the effective variety of the set is slightly smaller than the sample count suggests.

competency_alignment.rationale: The mathematics matches the competency, but the money facts do not always match Philippine currency, which matters on a node whose own sentence names money. Nine samples use a bills-and-coins frame with a peso amount that cannot be formed from any Philippine banknote: seed 42 'has ₱1 in bills and ₱40 in coins', seed 51 'has ₱19 in bills and ₱0 in coins', seed 604 'has ₱15 in bills and ₱20 in coins', and seed 601 'has ₱43 in bills and ₱0 in coins'. The smallest note in circulation is 20 pesos, so 1, 15, 19 and 43 pesos in bills teach a false denomination fact to the same pupils who are learning denominations. The denomination-tally items, seed 44 and seed 602, are accurate and show the correct pattern.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The largest operand is 500 pesos, at seed 602 'What is the total value of 1 ₱500 bill, 1 ₱20 bill, and 2 ₱1 coins?', and the largest sum is 522, both inside the sums-up-to-1000 bound. Values above the bound appear only as distractors and never as operands, namely 5220 at seed 602 and 1210 at seed 45. Realism note within range: seed 50 says 'has ₱5 in bills and ₱200 in coins', and 200 pesos entirely in coins is an odd quantity for a child to hold.
